accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:capped-capacity
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The clinical interpretation of B+W≤H is assumed as an externally prespecified finite-reserve sensitivity restriction, not established for SPRINT or implied by separate capping.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All sharpness, regret, and confidence claims are conditional on the externally justified capacity-sensitivity class M_H.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 1 equates the switched and sustained-standard post-landmark recurrent-count increment distributions conditional on survival, and the paper studies value and regret for switching regimes.
The publication characterizes nonempty fixed-margin transportation classes with staircase support and gives construction algorithms.

The paper proves a myopic greatest-cumulative-flow and maximum-reward result under lattice-superadditive rewards and cumulative capacities; it does not itself state arbitrary signed coefficient optimization.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2312.17623, precursor to the cited Review of Economic Studies article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies decision theory and minimax-regret rules for partially identified treatment-choice problems in a Gaussian-likelihood framework.
The article constructs identified-set estimators and confidence regions through inversion of a sample criterion under partial identification.
The publication studies regularized support-function inference for sharp polygonal affine identified sets, including uniform behavior at flat faces.
The identified article is published in volume 30, issue 1, pages 59–118 and develops counterfactual recurrent-event estimands; the core's volume-29/pages-759–778 citation is not this source.

The arXiv identifier resolves to Baer, Strawderman, and Ertefaie's 'Causal inference for the expected number of recurrent events in the presence of a terminal event,' which develops CAR identification, an efficiency bound, and multiply robust estimation; it is not the five-author/title record in the core.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct the two erroneous bibliography records and update every standard-assumption cite to the exact publication version and locator before Stage 0.

Add a formal corollary identifying a scientifically interpretable subclass of finite-reserve recurrent processes that satisfies B+W≤H, separating the conditional sensitivity result from any SPRINT-specific claim.

Promote the common-law tightening into a generic decision-class comparison, or add a second named clinical-policy comparator, to make the field-level advance less dependent on one scalar-bound baseline.

recommended_next_step: Repair the two standard-assumption citations, retain the accepted conditional capacity scope, then advance the field-level transport-and-common-law kernel to Stage 0.
